# UnpackedNamedArgumentCollision

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" /> <Badge type="info" text="PHP ≥ 8.0" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Detect an explicit or unpacked argument binding a parameter already certainly bound by a literal unpacked array on the same call.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
function send($id) {} send(...['id'=>7],id:8);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Bind each argument only once.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Report an explicit or unpacked argument binding a parameter already certainly bound by a literal unpacked array on the same call.
- Model PHP's argument counter when assigning positional values: a positional value takes the slot after the highest parameter slot filled so far, whether that slot was filled positionally or by name. A name collected by a variadic parameter fills no slot and leaves the counter unchanged.
- Resolve builtin calls and named arguments before checking the contract. Project-local callees are considered only when their bodies or immutable summaries establish the required facts. The default is enabled, with positive proof required.
- For flow-dependent conditions, require a reachable source-to-use path with no intervening invalidation. Unknown calls, ambiguous aliases, recursion or analysis-budget exhaustion cannot establish definite facts.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Unknown spreads, conditional keys, valid disjoint bindings and variadic distinct-name collection are excluded.
- A positional unpacked array following a named unpacked array is not a collision by itself: its values land after the named slot. Only a later argument naming a slot that was really filled is reported.
- A positional value reaching a variadic parameter or a slot beyond the declared parameters binds no name, and a positional element following a named element inside the same unpacked array raises a different runtime error; neither establishes a collision and analysis of the call stops there.
- Unresolved targets, incomplete required facts, suppressed findings and PHP versions lacking the referenced API or language feature produce no report. User declarations shadowing builtin names are not builtin contracts.

## Fix

No automatic fix: choosing which value to retain is application intent.

## PHP versions

Available from PHP 8.0. Builtin behavior and argument contracts follow the configured PHP version. Extension-specific calls require resolved extension API symbols; do not treat same-named application functions as extension calls.

## Options

None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "UnpackedNamedArgumentCollision": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore UnpackedNamedArgumentCollision
```
